_meta.what_this_is: A service receiving a shutdown signal (a deploy, a scale-down) while it has in-flight requests still being processed and new requests still arriving. Each in-flight request needs some more ticks of work to finish. A graceful shutdown DRAINS: stop accepting new requests (reject them cleanly so the client retries another instance), let the in-flight ones finish up to a drain deadline, then exit. A hard shutdown just exits now, dropping every in-flight request -- those clients get a connection error and their work is lost. The drain deadline bounds the wait: a request still running past it is force-terminated, so shutdown cannot hang forever.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. ticks_remaining per in-flight request and the drain_deadline are hand-authored so the completed, force-dropped, and hard-dropped counts are exact and checkable.
_meta.format: drain_deadline (ticks); in_flight [{id, ticks_remaining}]; new_requests (count arriving during shutdown)
